scope.quote: Nested multicall desyncs _isMulticall, breaking payment checks mid-batch

`Covenant.multicall` sets a contract-wide `_isMulticall` guard to `true` before delegating into `MulticallLib.multicall` and unconditionally clears it to `false` once the delegatecall returns ([`src/Covenant.sol:516-519`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-10-covenant/blob/main/src/Covenant.sol#L516-L519)). The library processes each payload item via `Address.functionDelegateCall(address(this), data)` ([`src/libraries/MultiCall.sol:21-24`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-10-covenant/blob/main/src/libraries/MultiCall.sol#L21-L24)), which means an inner payload can invoke `Covenant.multicall` again. The nested invocation flips `_isMulticall` back to `true`, but when the nested batch unwinds

it resets the flag to `false` while the outer batch is still iterating. Subsequent outer calls therefore execute with `_isMulticall == false` even though they are still part of the original multicall.

Payment-sensitive entrypoints like `updateState`, `mint`, `redeem`, and `swap` rely on `_checkPayment(msgValue)` to skip `msg.value == msgValue` enforcement during batched execution ([`src/Covenant.sol:556-559`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-10-covenant/blob/main/src/Covenant.sol#L556-L559)). Once the flag desynchronizes, the remaining batch items begin enforcing the equality check mid-flight and deterministically revert with `Errors.E_IncorrectPayment`. Any batch that nests `multicall`—even indirectly through helper calls—breaks for the remainder of the outer sequence. This is a reliable denial-of-service condition affecting multicall composability rather than a funds-draining bug.

outer_batch_items_revert.quote: - Nested multicalls cause outer batch items that follow the nested invocation to revert with `Errors.E_IncorrectPayment`, halting execution and wasting gas.

integrations_griefed.quote: - Integrations that rely on delegated batching (e.g., routers that compose protocol actions) can be griefed by inserting a nested `multicall`, turning otherwise valid sequences into guaranteed reverts.

dos_persists_no_recovery.quote: - Because the final balance check only triggers after the outer batch finishes, the DoS effect persists for the remainder of the transaction without any post-hoc recovery.
